globe.api:
OV.GlobeRender (js/gfx/globe_render.js). All pixel values are CSS px. Reads G and never writes it.

VIEW OBJECT (owned by the UI; draw() and the animation helpers write only lon, lat and zoom):
  lon, lat      globe centre in degrees; lat is clamped to ±89.
  zoom          0..5, fractional allowed. Radius = ZOOM_RADII interpolated geometrically × h.
  w, h, dpr     CSS size and device pixel ratio of the target canvas. The canvas must be round(w·dpr) × round(h·dpr).
  cx?, cy?      globe centre on screen; defaults w/2, h/2. Use these to offset the globe for a side panel.
  time          ms (performance.now()). Drives blink/pulse/dash animations and camera animations.
  selection     {kind,id} | null. Rotating dashed ring with brackets. kind 'country' outlines that country strongly.
  hover         {kind,id} | null. Thin ring. In 'target' mode the cursor snaps to the hovered object.
  highlights    [{kind,id}]. Attention pings, e.g. a newly detected UFO. kind 'country' outlines that country.
  country?      countryId | null. Hover outline plus label; any id in OV.Data.world.countries works.
  mode          'normal' | 'placeBase' | 'target'.
  cursor        {lon,lat} | null. The geo point under the pointer (from pick). Used by placeBase and target.
  placeValid?   boolean override for placeBase. Default is OV.Data.world.isLand(cursor).
  targetFrom?   {lon,lat} | null. In target mode, draws a dashed great-circle preview from here to the cursor or the hovered object.
  t?            game seconds for the sun when G is null, e.g. the new-game base placement.
  touch?        true widens hit radii to 22 px (default 14 px).
  showRadar? / showGrid? / labels?   default true.

DRAWING
  ZOOM_RADII = [0.45, 0.60, 0.90, 1.40, 2.25, 3.60]
  PAL        the palette, 0xRRGGBB integers.
  draw(ctx, G|null, view) → {ms, base:bool, light:bool}
      Draws the whole frame, including space and stars, and clears everything itself.
      It also advances any rotateTo/zoomTo/fling animation, using view.time.
      The sun position comes from OV.Clock.sunLon/declination(G.t).

QUERIES
  pick(view, px, py) → {lon, lat} | null           null when the point is in space.
  project(view, lon, lat) → {x, y, front}          front=false means the far side of the globe.
  visible(view, lon, lat) → bool
  radius(view) → px
  objectAt(G, view, px, py) → {kind, id} | null
      kind is one of 'ufo' (flying, landed and crashed UFO records), 'site' (terror), 'base', 'craft' (airborne only), 'alienBase', 'city'.
      Cities count only at zoom ≥ 2.75. G may be null, in which case only cities are returned.
      Only visible things are hit: detected UFOs or crashed ones (all UFOs if G.debug.revealUfos), discovered alien bases, front side only.
      Priority within 5 px: ufo > site > craft > alienBase > base > city.
  objectsAt(G, view, px, py) → [{kind, id, d}]     everything in reach, nearest first; use it for stacked objects.
  countryAt(view, px, py) → countryId | null       real outlines, via OV.Data.world.countryAt(…, 1).
  screenPos(G, view, {kind, id}) → {x, y, front} | null
      Accepts kinds ufo / site / base / craft / alienBase / city / {kind:'point', lon, lat}.
  radarCircles(G) → [{lon, lat, rangeNm, kind, baseId|craftId}]
      Uses OV.World.radarCircles(G) when that exists. Otherwise it computes completed base radar facilities plus airborne crafts.

CAMERA (each one mutates view.lon / lat / zoom)
  rotateBy(view, dx, dy)
      Drag or two-finger scroll: Δlon = −dx/R, Δlat = +dy/R, lat clamped to ±89. Cancels any running rotation or fling.
  zoomAt(view, zoom, px?, py?)
      Instant zoom that keeps the geo point under (px,py) fixed. Use it for pinch or Ctrl+wheel.
  zoomTo(view, zoom, ms=280, px?, py?)       animated zoom; the anchor is optional.
  rotateTo(view, lon, lat, ms?, zoom?)
      Animated slerp with ease-in-out. Default duration is 450–900 ms depending on distance. Long trips briefly zoom out ("fly").
      ms = 0 jumps immediately. Use it for auto-centring on events and double-click / Option-click.
  fling(view, vxPxPerMs, vyPxPerMs)          inertia after a drag release; decays exponentially (τ = 260 ms).
  stop(view)                                 cancels all camera animation.
  update(view, now?) → bool                  still animating? draw() calls this too.
  busy(view) → bool
      True while animating, or while the frame was drawn coarse during motion and the fine cached frame is not built yet.
      Keep the rAF loop going while it is true.

MAINTENANCE
  prewarm()      builds geometry plus the 0.5° biome and ocean textures, about 100–300 ms once. Call it on entering the scene to avoid a first-draw hitch.
  invalidate()   drops all caches.

MARKER SEMANTICS
  bases        blue squares; name at zoom ≥ 2.
  crafts       chevrons pointing along the great-circle heading. Interceptors amber, transports green. Dashed path to dest (dimmer when returning). Orbit ring when on patrol. Name at zoom ≥ 3.
  flying UFOs  red blinking blips, radius 2.6 + 0.9·size, with a radar ping. Undetected UFOs (debug reveal only) are drawn hollow.
  landed UFOs  yellow diamond with a pulse.
  crashed UFOs orange ⊗.
  terror sites red skull with a double pulse; city name always shown.
  alien bases  purple hexagon.
  radars       dashed circles (base teal, hyper-wave violet, craft amber thin) with a faint fill.
  edge arrows  at the limb or screen edge for off-view flying UFOs, terror sites, the selection and highlights.
  labels       placed by priority without overlaps: selection, hover, site, base, ufo, craft, city.
  placeBase    valid/invalid colour, small-radar preview circle (1695 nm), country under the cursor outlined.
globe.summary:
I built the Geoscape globe renderer: `OV.GlobeRender` in `js/gfx/globe_render.js`. It covers everything in the brief except the confirmed ≥55 fps: this container has no GPU, so frame rate could only be measured in software. My new tests pass (7), and the full strict suite is green: 527 passed, 0 failed.

**What it draws**
- **Globe and land:** an orthographic globe with Natural Earth land. I used the limb-collapse plus antipode-parity fill from the REA, densified edges to ≤ 2° and precomputed the unit vectors. The ±180° cut is nudged, and tests check the land fill against the land mask.
- **Ocean and terrain:** ocean and land colours come from a per-pixel pass over 0.5° textures built once at load.
  - The ocean is lighter on the shallow shelf near coasts and darker offshore.
  - Land is coloured by latitude, with desert, mountain and jungle taken from the terrain boxes in the data files, plus ice caps and Greenland.
  - Coastlines stay crisp because the land texture is clipped to the land outline.
- **Light and atmosphere:**
  - The real sun position at `G.t` drives the day/night line, with a soft warm twilight.
  - Limb darkening and blue haze on the day side; the outer glow fades out on the night side.
  - A sun glint on the ocean, stars and a faint graticule.
  - City lights: clusters around the 53 cities, on land only, shown on the night side.
- **Markers and overlays:** the dynamic layer draws everything listed in the brief, as described in the API field. Additions beyond the brief:
  - Arrows at the globe edge or screen edge for UFOs, terror sites and the selection when they are out of view.
  - Labels placed by priority so they never overlap or run off-screen.
  - Inertia after a drag (`fling`) and a brief zoom-out during long `rotateTo` trips.

**Performance**
- **How it works:** while the camera moves, it draws straight to the screen at a coarser sampling step. When it stops (260 ms), it builds a fine cached base and light layer. An idle frame is then one copy plus the markers.
- **Container measurements** (1440×900 @2×, Chromium without a GPU, CPU shared with five other engineers):

| Case | JS time per frame | Frame rate here |
|---|---|---|
| Rotating | ~11 ms median | 5–8 fps |
| Idle, 50+ markers | 1.2 ms | 44 fps |
| Clock running (sun moving every frame) | ~54 ms | 13 fps |

- **Why fps is low here:** even with every layer switched off, only 22–26 fps is reached, so the low numbers come from software rendering in this container.
- **On a Mac:** I expect the target to be met, since the JS work is small and the raster operations are cheap with a GPU, but this needs checking on a real Mac.
- **Avoided:** no `ctx.filter` and no `OffscreenCanvas`.

**Visual QA:** I looked at the screenshots and iterated over 4 rounds. Fixes included the night-scene clock, a softer terminator, label collisions, a narrower coastal shelf and brighter night land. The final 13 screenshots are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-HelloWorld/b8cfbac1-629a-5f58-8dfb-0f752cc84b7c/scratchpad/ui4/globe/`. They cover:
- day over Europe and night over Asia;
- dusk over the Atlantic;
- city zoom and maximum zoom;
- base placement on land (valid) and at sea (invalid);
- target mode and many objects;
- the South Pole, the Pacific and the Arctic.

**Browser checks** (`qa/globe_check.mjs`, 27/27):
- `pick` of `project` returns the same point (error below 1e-10 nm).
- `objectAt`, `countryAt`, `rotateTo`, `zoomAt` anchoring and real mouse drag all behave correctly.
- No console errors.
- The server ran on a random port and was stopped.

**Tests** (`tools/tests/gfx_globe.test.js`, 7): zoom radii, projection round-trips including the poles, culling, object picking (priority, hidden UFOs, far side, toggles), radar circles, camera animation and a full draw with a fake canvas.
deviations: Additions beyond the requested API, all listed in the api field: objectsAt (every object in reach, for stacked markers), countryAt, screenPos, radius, visible, radarCircles, rotateBy, zoomAt, fling, stop, update, busy, prewarm, invalidate and PAL. There are also optional view fields: cx/cy, cursor, placeValid, targetFrom, country, t, touch, showRadar, showGrid, labels.

Landed and crashed UFOs are returned by objectAt as kind 'ufo', because they are UFO records in the contract. Only terror sites are kind 'site'. They are drawn as site-style markers: yellow for landed, orange for crashed.

Radar circles come from OV.World.radarCircles when that exists. world.js was still a placeholder, so there is a fallback: completed base radar facilities plus airborne crafts (Data.crafts.radarRange). Both give the same shape.

draw() advances camera animations from view.time and may change view.lon, view.lat and view.zoom; it never touches G. The terrain colours inside land are cosmetic, built from OV.Data.terrainBoxes plus latitude bands; they are not the battle terrain rules.

Map labels (base, craft, city, terror city, UFO size or type, country names on hover) are drawn on the canvas using existing OV.T keys: base.defaultName, craft.instance, city.*, country.*, ufo.* and ufo.size.*. No new i18n keys were needed.
open_issues: Frame rate at 1440×900 @2× could not be confirmed in this container: Chromium has no GPU here, and even an almost empty frame of this harness only reaches 22–26 fps. Measured JS time per frame: rotating 11 ms median, idle with 50+ markers 1.2 ms, light re-render about 54 ms here (mostly software full-canvas copies). Please run `node ovni-1999/qa/globe_check.mjs` on a real Mac in Safari and Chrome to confirm ≥ 55 fps while rotating.

Natural Earth 1:110m outlines look angular at zoom 4–5 (France and Italy are coarse polygons). Raising detail would mean regenerating js/data/world.js with tools/build_world.mjs from the 1:50m set. That file is not mine and the data would grow about 10×.

Notes for the Geoscape UI engineer:
- Call GlobeRender.prewarm() when entering the scene (one-time texture build of 100–300 ms).
- Keep requestAnimationFrame running while GlobeRender.busy(view) is true or any UFO or terror site is visible, because of the blink and ping animations.
- Throttle draws to ≤ 10 Hz when nothing animates (contract §6.3).
- Set view.cursor from pick() on pointermove, needed for base placement and target modes.
- Use objectsAt when several objects share a spot (e.g. a craft shadowing a UFO).

The light layer re-renders only when the sun moves at least 0.1° (24 s of game time), so at the 5-s speed the day/night line updates about every 2 s of real time, and every step at faster speeds. No action needed; noted for tuning.

The full test suite was green at the end (527/527). Other engineers' modified files in the tree at that time: crafts.js, tuning.js, campaign.js, base.js, world.js, the dogfight files and base_render.js. None of them broke the globe tests or the QA script.

baseart.api: OV.BaseRender = { draw(ctx, base, view) — ctx already in CSS px (as OV.View.begin); never mutates base/G. view = { x, y, cell, dpr, time?, hover:{x,y}|null, selection:{x,y}|null, ghost:{type,x,y,valid}|null, dismantle:{x,y,ok?}|null (ok:false = refused, amber), highlight:type|[type]|null, G | crafts:[craft|{type,status}|null] in base.crafts order } cellAt(view, px, py) -> {x,y}|null layout(w, h, {pad=12,minCell=28,maxCell=112}?) -> {x, y, cell} (whole-number cell, grid centred) facilityAt(base, x, y) -> grid entry|null (any cell of a 2x2 hangar) facilityRect(view, entry) -> {x,y,w,h} CSS px hangarSlots(base, view?) -> [{x,y,craftId,craft}] finished hangars in grid order; craft i of base.crafts sits in hangar i animated(base) -> bool ; ANIM_FPS = 20 (UI should redraw at ~20 Hz while true) facilityIcon(type, size, dpr=1) -> NEW canvas (size*dpr px; 2x2 hangar scaled to fit) craftIcon(type, size, dpr=1) -> NEW canvas facilityIconURL(type,size,dpr) / craftIconURL(type,size,dpr) -> cached PNG data URL for hasArt(type), hasCraftArt(type), TYPES, CRAFT_TYPES, clearCache(), stats() -> {entries,pixels,staticKey}, setCanvasFactory(fn) }
baseart.summary:
Implemented OV.BaseRender (js/gfx/base_render.js), procedural top-down cut-away art for the Basescape.
- Background: rock/earth texture under the 6x6 grid (noise computed once at CSS resolution, then pebbles, cracks and excavation corner marks); corridors drawn automatically between orthogonally adjacent facilities.
- Facilities: unique art for all 13 facilities in OV.Data.facilities plus the P2 ones (fusion defence, grav shield, mind shield, psi lab). Generic room for unknown types.
- Hangars: 2x2 landing pad with the parked craft drawn by type (Skyranger, Interceptor, Firestorm, Avenger, generic fallback), with a built-in drop shadow. A craft that is out is not drawn; repair/rearm/refuel shows blinking service lights.
- Containment: alien silhouettes per pen from base.aliens.
- Construction: dug-up ground, a concrete slab and the facility sprite revealed left to right with progress, blueprint outline, scaffolding, materials, blinking beacon, days-left badge (clock glyph + number, no i18n needed) and a progress bar.
- Interaction: hover outline (cyan), selection brackets (amber), highlight-by-type (teal), dismantle overlay (red X or amber refused symbol), ghost placement green/red with marching-ants outline, hatched when invalid, clipped to the grid.
- Animation: rotating radar dishes with a sweep wedge, flickering lab screens and rotating hologram, containment force-field glow, turret sweep with lens/plasma/fusion glow, hyper-wave/grav/mind/psi ripples, chasing lift and hangar pad lights, workshop crane and welding sparks.
- Palette from css/base.css tokens and the battlescape CRAFT tileset, lit from the top-left like the battlescape tiles.
- Caching: per-facility sprite cache plus a cached static layer (rock + corridors + facilities + construction) keyed by grid signature, cell and dpr. A warm frame takes about 1.6 ms in headless Chromium; the cold first draw about 90 ms.
- QA: qa/base_check.mjs (Playwright, file://, no server) renders the newCampaign starting base, a full late-game base, construction states, ghost valid/invalid/off-grid, dismantle, type highlight, icon sheet and an animation strip. It checks no console/page errors, that animation changes 3.35 % of pixels, that the same time gives the same image, cellAt/layout/hangarSlots, that base is not mutated, and frame timing. Three visual rounds: removed a stray line on the Firestorm, brightened the psi-lab chairs, and replaced the graph-paper construction look with a single left-to-right sweep (excavation, slab, scaffolding, materials). Passes at DPR 2 cell 72 and DPR 1 cell 56.
- Node tests: tools/tests/gfx_base_render.test.js, 7 tests in about 0.23 s with a validating mock canvas. Full --strict suite: 425 pass, 1 fail; the failure is not in my files (see open issues).
deviations: The view object goes beyond the brief with optional fields: dismantle {x,y,ok?} (the brief said 'dismantle highlight' without a shape), highlight (type or list), and G or crafts so hangared craft can be drawn, since draw(ctx, base, view) only receives the base and crafts live in G.crafts.

Which craft sits in which hangar is an assumption: craft i of base.crafts occupies the i-th finished hangar in grid order. The contract only says base.crafts is in 'roster / hangar order'. Exposed as hangarSlots() so the UI can map hangar clicks to crafts.

facilityIcon/craftIcon take an extra optional dpr argument and return a fresh canvas copy on every call, so the same icon can be inserted into several DOM lists. Cached data-URL variants (facilityIconURL/craftIconURL) were added for use.
The days-left badge is a drawn clock glyph plus the number, so no new i18n keys are needed (I don't own pt-PT.base.js).
open_issues: The full --strict suite has 1 failure outside my files: data_crossref.test.js 'textos em pt-PT sem formas brasileiras comuns' flags up.archive and up.menu.hint (the Ufopaedia engineer's in-progress i18n).

For the base_ui engineer: redraw the basescape canvas at about OV.BaseRender.ANIM_FPS (20 Hz) while OV.BaseRender.animated(base) is true; stop redrawing when idle. Pass view.dismantle.ok = (OV.BaseSim.canDismantle(...) === null) and ghost.valid = (OV.BaseSim.canPlace(...) === null).
If BaseSim ever tracks a per-craft hangar assignment instead of using base.crafts order, hangarSlots() in base_render.js should read it.
